summary: Dungkar Lozang Trinlé (1927–1997) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera and Gyuto monasteries under Ngawang Yönten. He held posts at Minzu University (~1960–1965), Tibet University (~1985–1997), and the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (~1985–1997).

Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya (1899–1965) was an Indologist educated at Vidyasagar College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta. He held teaching posts at Narasinha Dutt College, Scottish Church College, Sanskrit College and University (1952), and the University of Calcutta (~1957–1965).
Durga Prasad Dikshit is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under teachers R. K. Dikshit and Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi, and completed his doctoral studies under Baij Nath Puri.
Dwijendra Narayan Jha (1940–2021) was an Indologist and historian. He completed his studies at Presidency College, Kolkata (~1957–1961), Patna University (~1961–1964), and the University of Calcutta.

Dylan Esler is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from SOAS University of London and completed his PhD in 2018 at the Catholic University of Louvain, where he also served as a research scholar.

Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, and Khenpo Rinchen, and was a professor of Buddhist philosophy at Naropa University in 1990.

Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He served as director of the Nitartha Institute (~1996) and Kamalashila Institute (attested 2013).

Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sakya College and SOAS University of London under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Dudjom Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Sakya Trizin, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje.

Dzongsar Khyentse 02 studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang. His notable students included Shenphen Nangwa, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje.

Dzongsar Khyentse Chokyi Lodro (1893–1959) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Khenpo Thupten, Shechen Gyaltsap Gyurme Pema Namgyal, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and succeeded Dzongsar Khyentse Jamyang Chökyi Wangpo.
Dániel Balogh is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the British Museum (attested 2021) and as a visiting lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).

Dörte Kamarid is a scholar in Tibetology and Indology. She studied at the University of Vienna, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, completing an MA under the supervision of Helmut Tauscher.

E. D. Hirsch is a philosopher and scholar educated at Metairie Park Country Day School and Cornell University (~1946–1950). He held academic posts at Wesleyan University (~1966–1969) and the University of Virginia (~1966–2012).

E. F. Schumacher (1911–1977) was a philosopher. He studied under Edward Conze and attended New College, Columbia University, the University of Bonn, and the London School of Economics. He held academic posts at Columbia University (~1930–1932) and the University of Oxford.

E. Gene Smith (1936–2010) was a Tibetologist who studied at Adelphi, Hobart and William Smith, Utah, and Washington under Turrell V. Wylie, Dezhung Rinpoche, and Dilgo Khyentse. He held posts at the Library of Congress and the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

E. W. Adikaram (1905–1985) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Wesley College, the University of Colombo, SOAS, and the University of London under William Stede. In 1934, he served as principal of Ananda Sastralaya, Kotte.

Eberhard Fischer is a scholar of Indology and archaeology who earned his PhD from the University of Basel (~1960–1965). He served as director of Museum Rietberg (1972–1998) and later held posts with the Rietberg Society and the Swiss-Liechtenstein Foundation.

Eberhard Sandschneider is a sinologist who completed his education and PhD at Saarland University (~1976–1986). He held posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1995–1998), Free University of Berlin (1999–2001), and the German Council on Foreign Relations (2003–2016).

Eberhard Schrader (1836–1908) was a scholar of linguistics and history who studied at the University of Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald (~1854–1858). He held posts at Zurich, Giessen, Jena, and the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1875–1908).

Edeltraud Harzer is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She studied at Charles University, the University of Washington, and under traditional teachers Shree Narayan Mishra and Ram Shankar Bhattacharya. She held posts at Puget Sound, Washington, Stanford, Indiana, and Texas at Austin.
